title: Scarlet Monastery
body: The Scarlet Monastery stands in the hills of northeastern Tirisfal, above the gardens where the Scarlet Crusade keeps its watch. Before the plague it was a house of Lordaeron's priesthood, where the faithful came to study and to seek the Light. After the Scourge overran the kingdom in the Third War, the Crusade made it a fortress, and it is now the order's great seat in the glades. Its zealots hold that any outsider may carry the plague, and they meet intruders swearing that the Light condemns all who harbor evil. From the vestibule four ways lead in: to the graveyard where prisoners suffer and the dead do not rest, to the library, to the armory and its training halls, and to the cathedral at the monastery's heart. Scarlet Commander Mograine leads the soldiers of the cathedral, but the monastery's true master is said to be High Inquisitor Whitemane. The Forsaken want its zealots dead, and scholars far away send for the books on its shelves.

title: The Graveyard
body: The Graveyard wing begins in the Chamber of Atonement, and the name is a cruel one. Scarlet torturers work there among wretched undead captives, and their talk is all of confession: confess and be set free, they say, for everyone talks in the end, though one will admit he does not care what is said, since he simply enjoys inflicting pain. Interrogator Vishas keeps his post among them. Beyond lies the Forlorn Cloister, a graveyard where nothing rests. Restless spirits drift between the graves, rotting corpses walk and phantasms haunt the dark, and at the far end stairs lead down into the crypts of Honor's Tomb.

parts.body: Below the stairs at the graveyard's far end, Bloodmage Thalnos rose to meet intruders, a skeletal mage who cried that the dead hunger for vengeance. He hurled bolts of shadow, called down pillars of flame, seared his foes with fire and burst outward in a ring of flame. Wounded, he cried that there is no rest for the angry dead. But the bloodmage fell at last, among the dead he spoke for.

title: The Library
body: The Library wing holds the Huntsman's Cloister, the Gallery of Treasures and the Athenaeum. Near the way in, Scarlet gallants and beastmasters keep packs of tracking hounds, and further on, monks, chaplains and diviners stand watch among long tables and reading stands. The books laid out on them are histories of the world: the War of the Ancients, the World Tree and the Emerald Dream, Arathor and the troll wars, and darker chapters, it is said, wait in the farther halls where the library's keeper walks.

parts.body: One book on these shelves came by a strange road. Rituals of Power was written by the Magus Tirth, once a great mage and scholar, who has traded his studies for ale and wagers at the races of the Shimmering Flats. Gambling debts drove him to sell the last copy to one of the Scarlet clergy, and he has no doubt it ended up in the monastery's library.

title: The Armory
body: The Armory wing is where the Crusade drills and arms its soldiers. Its halls are the Training Grounds, the Footman's Armory and the Crusader's Armory, held by soldiers, guardsmen and protectors, evokers, myrmidons and defenders, with crates of armor and weapons among them. At the far end a heavy door opens on the Hall of Champions, where plaques honor the order's heroes.

title: The Cathedral
body: The Cathedral wing is the heart of the monastery. Its way leads through the Chapel Gardens, held by sorcerers, wizards, centurions, myrmidons and defenders, to the doors of the Crusader's Chapel. Every wing of the monastery keeps its own road, but this one leads to those who command the rest, and its guards are the order's best. Within the chapel the order's commanders keep their seats and its abbots, monks and chaplains keep the nave.

title: High Inquisitor Whitemane
body: High Inquisitor Whitemane is a priestess of the Light and, by every account, the true master of the Scarlet Monastery. Scarlet Commander Mograine leads the soldiers of the cathedral, but it is Whitemane who directs the Crusade's work from within its walls, and she is spoken of as a fearsome woman. She keeps to her own chambers behind the Crusader's Chapel, beyond the High Inquisitor's Door at the commander's back, with a staff in her hand and the chapel between her and any intruder.

parts.body: When Mograine fell, the door behind him swung open and Whitemane came out crying that Mograine had fallen, that the intruders would pay for this treachery. She smote her foes with holy fire and shielded those beside her, until she cast a deep sleep over everyone near her and went to the fallen commander. Arise, my champion, she called, and he rose. Then she fought at his side, healing him and bending her foes' minds to her will, until at last she fell.

title: Scarlet Commander Mograine
body: Scarlet Commander Mograine leads the warriors of the Scarlet Monastery, a large garrison of fanatically devoted soldiers. He stands at the far end of the Crusader's Chapel, a tall man with a great two-handed mace, and the abbots, monks and champions who fill the chapel are his to call on. The door at his back leads to the chambers of High Inquisitor Whitemane, and no one reaches her except past him.

parts.body: Mograine met intruders crying that the infidels must be purified, and the whole chapel rose to fight beside him. He struck with crusading blows, stunned foes with the hammer of justice, and his aura burned all who struck him. Beaten down, he fell as if dead. Whitemane came for him, and at her call he rose again, crying At your side, milady, and laid healing hands upon her. He fought on until he fell a second time, and this time he did not rise.

title: Herod
body: Herod bears the title of the Scarlet Champion, and he keeps to the one hall in the monastery named for such men. He waits at the far end of the Armory wing in the Hall of Champions, beneath the plaques that honor the Crusade's fallen heroes, a towering man with a great two-handed axe. The soldiers and defenders of the training halls stand between him and the door, and those who make war on the Crusade name him among the monastery's leaders.

parts.body: Herod met intruders glad of a real challenge at last. He cleaved through those beside him and spun into a whirlwind of steel, crying Blades of light. Badly wounded, he called on the Light to give him strength and flew into a rage. Yet the Scarlet Champion fell. As he died, a crowd of Scarlet trainees poured into the hall, crying that the master had fallen and calling on their brethren to avenge him.

title: Houndmaster Loksey
body: Houndmaster Loksey keeps the Crusade's hounds in the Library wing, not far from the way in. Tracking hounds lie close about him, and the Scarlet beastmasters nearby keep more of them, for the Crusade uses such dogs to hunt down its enemies. He carries an axe in each hand and does not stray from his pack. Whoever means to reach the books and the arcanist beyond must first get past the houndmaster and his dogs.

parts.body: Loksey met intruders with a cry of Release the hounds, and the tracking hounds around him leapt to the attack. He drove them on with a battle fury that quickened their bites while he cut at his foes with his two axes. Neither the dogs nor their master could hold, and the houndmaster fell among his pack.

title: Arcanist Doan
body: Arcanist Doan is the keeper of the monastery's library, a mage of the Scarlet Crusade among its priests and warriors. He walks the farthest hall of the Library wing, staff in hand, along the reading stands where the histories of the Scourge lie open, and a strongbox stands close by his path. Monks and chaplains keep watch around him, but the books, and whatever the order guards among them, are his charge.

parts.body: Doan met intruders crying that they would not defile these mysteries. He loosed blasts of arcane power, silenced those who would cast spells and turned his foes into sheep. Wounded, he wrapped himself in a bubble of arcane force, then let it burst in a detonation, crying Burn in righteous fire. It did not save him, and the keeper of the library fell among his books.

title: High Inquisitor Fairbanks
body: Off the Crusader's Chapel, behind a secret door that a torch upon the wall opens, lies a hidden room, and in it waits High Inquisitor Fairbanks. He bears the same title as the monastery's mistress, yet he has no place among the zealots of the chapel and keeps no door they pass through. Whoever finds him will find him ready, a hammer in his hand. What he once was, and why he lingers in that hidden place, the chapel does not say.

parts.body: Those who opened the hidden room found what it kept from the chapel: Fairbanks is undead, one of the very dead the Crusade has sworn to destroy, yet he fought for the Crusade still. He fought with a priest's magic, laying a curse of blood on his foes that made every blow against them bite deeper, stripping away the magic that guarded them, wrapping himself in a shield of light and healing his own wounds. None of it was enough, and the undead inquisitor fell in his hidden room.

title: Down the Scarlet Path
body: Brother Anton of Nijel's Point has a reward for those who prove themselves against the undead of Desolace: a place in the Scarlet Crusade's work in Lordaeron. He speaks proudly of what his order holds there, a chain of strongholds running from Hearthglen to Tirisfal Glades, each a bastion where the land is cleansed. To the worthy he gives a letter of commendation sealed with his own mark, and sends them across the sea to the town of Southshore. There a crusader called Raleigh the Devout is to receive the letter and take its bearer to the Scarlet Monastery, where Anton promises them a place of honor.

parts.body: In Southshore, Raleigh the Devout met the letter's bearer with suspicion, demanding to know who had come and what they wanted of him. Anton's seal brought no welcome. Raleigh seemed only dismayed to learn that the brother was still out preaching for the Scarlet Crusade.
sources: quest 1052 request text (Who goes there? What do you want from me?) and reward text (Brother Anton still spreads the word of the Scarlet Crusade? Oh my....); creature_questender 3980 Raleigh the Devout (map 0, area 271 Southshore)

parts.body: Raleigh had once been one of them. He served the Crusade faithfully and proudly, sure that ridding Azeroth of the undead was a noble cause. Time at the Monastery changed his mind: he watched its zealots lose their hold on reality, until anyone without the Crusade's tabard counted as plagued, and innocent men and women were tortured for it. Now he wants the order crushed in the Light's name, starting at the top: Whitemane, Mograine, Herod and Loksey.
sources: quest 1053 description (served the Scarlet Crusade with honor, loyalty and pride; a noble cause, to rid Azeroth of the undead; at the Monastery their grasp on reality was slipping; everyone who doesn't wear the tabard thought plagued; innocent men and women tortured; crushed in the name of the Light) and objectives (High Inquisitor Whitemane, Scarlet Commander Mograine, Herod, Houndmaster Loksey); AllowableRaces 1101, QuestType 2, Flags 8, PrevQuestID 1052

parts.body: Raleigh believed the rot in the Monastery would last as long as its highest officers did, and that only with them gone could the cause he once served be kindled anew. When word came that the four had fallen he did not rejoice, for a servant of the Light takes no pleasure in killing. Still, he held that such sacrifices are sometimes the price of the greater good, for the kingdom and for the world, and that many innocents would live because of what was done in the Monastery.
sources: quest 1053 request text (the corruption will not end until the highest ranking officials have been removed; perhaps the true cause can be rekindled) and reward text (disciples of the Light never revel in the loss of life; such sacrifices for the greater good of the Kingdom and the planet; spared many innocent lives); creature_questender 3980

title: Into the Scarlet Monastery
body: For the Forsaken, the Scarlet Crusade is a war fought on their own doorstep. Its zealots swarm over Tirisfal, hunting the dead wherever they walk, and their stronghold, the Scarlet Monastery, rises in the northeast of the glades. From the Royal Quarter of the Undercity an order goes out to strike at the root: go to the Monastery and kill High Inquisitor Whitemane, along with those who serve directly beneath her, Scarlet Commander Mograine, Herod the Scarlet Champion, and Houndmaster Loksey with his hounds.

parts.body: The order came from the dreadlord Varimathras. With the Dark Lady occupied by the Lich King's advance in the north, he had taken it upon himself to set the homeland in order, and no trouble at home galled him more than the human vermin of the Scarlet Crusade, whose red-clad zealots infest the glades. He wanted Whitemane and her chief lieutenants destroyed.
sources: quest 1048 description (whilst the Dark Lady tends to the pressing issue of the Lich King's advance to the north; matters closer to home; the human pests who call themselves the Scarlet Crusade, the sharpest thorn in our side domestically; Tirisfal crawling with the little red ants; lay waste to High Inquisitor Whitemane and her top lieutenants); creature_queststarter 2425 Varimathras

parts.body: Varimathras would settle for nothing short of Whitemane dead for good, and her commanders with her: the zealot Mograine, the champion Herod, and Loksey along with his dogs. When the deed was done, he conceded that it had been no easy errand. The Dark Lady had been served well, he declared; such loyalty to the Forsaken would not go unnoticed, nor would such stubbornness in battle be forgotten.
sources: quest 1048 request text (Whitemane killed once and for all; her top brass; that zealot Mograine; Herod; Loksey and his filthy mutts) and reward text (served the Dark Lady well; no small task; loyalty to the Forsaken noted; tenacity in combat remembered); creature_questender 2425

parts.body: In the Royal Quarter, the order was given by Bragor Bloodfist, an orc who counts helping the Forsaken guard their borders among his duties in the Undercity. His reasons were his own as well as theirs: he lives and breathes, yet the Crusade would slay his kind as readily as any of the undead. With Whitemane and her lieutenants slain, he was sure Sylvanas would welcome the news. It had been a hard task, he granted, and a victory like that earns respect.
sources: quest 14355 description (one of my duties while I'm stationed here is to help the Forsaken take care of their borders; I might live and breathe, but the Scarlet Crusade will cut down my people as quickly as one of the undead; a big problem; slay Whitemane and her lieutenants) and reward text (Sylvanas will be glad to have that problem taken care of; the task wasn't easy; victorious; commands respect, won't be forgotten); creature_queststarter/questender 36273 Bragor Bloodfist

title: Hearts of Zeal
body: In the Apothecarium, Master Apothecary Faranell has plans for the Kraul guano he sent for. He means to set two utterly opposed substances against each other, binding both with a lasting poison, and he expects results of the most horrific kind. The second substance must come from the Scarlet Crusade, whose fanatics crowd the Scarlet Monastery high in the northeast of Tirisfal Glades, in its halls and on its grounds alike. Any one of them may carry what he needs, so it makes no difference which of them fall. He wants twenty Hearts of Zeal.

parts.body: Faranell had waited eagerly for the hearts, for his delightful experiment would need a great many. When twenty Hearts of Zeal, cut from the Crusade's zealots, were set before him, he was overjoyed at so generous a heap of gore and praised the labor that had gathered it.

title: Mythology of the Titans
body: In the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, Librarian Mae Paledust of the Explorers' League believes no one can escape what is to come, but that those who know the past can face it better prepared. Before Lordaeron's troubles, she says, a great house of learning lay tucked away in Tirisfal Glades, and rumor holds that its library, in the old Monastery, kept a book called Mythology of the Titans. She wants it found and brought to her, so that together they may uncover the secrets of ages gone.

parts.body: Mae Paledust knew the old Monastery's story. Paladins once trained there, and it stood as a stronghold of the Light until the fanatics of the Scarlet Crusade took it. They thought their purpose noble, to cleanse the land of the undead plague, but madness crept into the cause, and now they are the enemies of everyone. Halls so corrupted were no fit home for so precious a record of the past. With the book recovered, she gave thanks on behalf of the League.
sources: quest 1050 request text (the Monastery was a seminary for Paladins-in-training; once a stronghold of the Light; fell into the hands of the crazed zealots of the Scarlet Crusade; a noble goal, to purify the land of the undead plague; insanity tainted their plight; enemies to all; the corrupt halls no place for such a historical treasure) and reward text (rescued the sacred text; thank you on behalf of the Explorers' League)

parts.body: The book begins where all things began. No one knows how the universe was born, it says, but a race of powerful beings arose to bring it order: the titans, colossal gods with skin of metal, who raised mountains, dredged seas and breathed skies into being. Ruled by the Pantheon, they ordered a hundred million worlds, ever watchful against the demons of the Twisting Nether.
sources: item 5536 Mythology of the Titans, PageText 575-578 (no one knows exactly how the universe began; the Titans, colossal, metallic-skinned gods; raised mountains, dredged seas, breathed skies into being; ruled by the Pantheon; a hundred million worlds; vigilant against the demonic beings of the Twisting Nether); looted from gameobject 19284, single spawn on map 189 at 281,-352 in the library
